comment: THE CAPABILITY x PROTOCOL EQUALITY MATRIX -- the equality doctrine, as a pinned instrument.
Owner's ruling (repeated; this file exists so it never has to be repeated again):
'breakers, hooks, auditing -- list all the core functionality. outside should ONLY BE
Auth, Store, Protocols, i.e. Plugins. Any plugin gets all functionality.
LLM == MCP == A2A -- just different protocols not different pathway through engine at all.'
Every CORE CAPABILITY x PROTOCOL PLANE cell is exactly one of:
proven          -- with `test`: `<repo-relative test file>::<test fn>`. The gate
(crates/busbar/tests/capability_equality.rs) verifies the file exists and
the fn is in it, so a proven cell cannot outlive its evidence.
missing         -- the capability does not reach this plane today, or no test proves it does.
A proof that nobody watched is a claim; MISSING is the honest state until
a named test exists. The missing set is the work queue, and every umbrella
run prints it (scripts/capability-equality-summary.py, wired into
cargo xtask full-gate) -- green stays green, but the gap is NAMED.
not-applicable  -- with `reason`: a one-line argument. N/A is a claim, not an escape; the
gate refuses an n/a cell whose argument is missing or trivial.
The capability list is the one-of-each modules in core -- each a mechanism that exists
exactly once and that every plane is owed:
breaker.rs, failover/, hooks/, audit/, governance/, metrics.rs, trust/, net_guard.rs,
bound_credential.rs (a lane credential bound on its style's auth plugin), catalogue.rs, and the disposition pipeline (proto/ Stage 1 -> breaker::classify).
CHANGING THIS FILE: close a cell by flipping it to `proven` WITH the test that proves it, in
the SAME commit as the test. Regressing a proven cell (its test vanishes or is renamed) is RED.
Adding a capability or plane without filling its whole row/column is RED (the cross product is
exact). Do not delete a capability to shrink the queue.
THE ROOT COLUMN (`root_legs` + every cell's `root`). The `test` above is the LEGACY path: the
capability proven where the plane crate serves it. Every plane now also runs through the
composition root -- root-llm (the root's node, behind plane-llm) / root-admin behind their features, root-mcp / root-a2a on the
kernel-loop rider every linked one-shot plane is served through, root-voice on its session rider -- and a
capability that holds on the legacy path and is unwitnessed over the loop is a second, silent
half of the same question. So each cell carries a SECOND verdict, over its plane's root leg:
proven          -- with `test`: a `<the leg's own file under crates/busbar/src/root/>::<test fn>` cell that
drives the capability through the leg. The gate verifies the file is the
leg's own file and the fn is in it.
none            -- with `reason`: the leg does not witness this capability yet, and the reason
says what the leg does instead. R-16: name a gap, never paper it.
not-applicable  -- the cell's own state is `not-applicable`, so the leg is owed nothing here.
The two states move together: a cell is n/a on both paths or on neither.
`root_legs` declares the legs and, per leg, the ledger columns it answers to and the cargo
`feature` that compiles it into a build. `dialects` names what a plane speaks inside itself and
is never a column. root-admin
answers to ZERO columns on purpose (admin is not one of the doctrine's protocol planes); its
root leg is judged by qa/teller-steps.json's cleanliness row 'cleanliness_rows.admin' instead.
The root column's evidence is verified for EXISTENCE by the gate on every build, and
RUN by `scripts/capability-equality-summary.py --root-legs`, which builds the binary crate with
every leg's feature on and executes every named root cell -- so `proven` on this column means the
instrument was watched over the loop, not only that it is on disk.

capabilities.breaker-trip: a failing upstream target records into the ONE core breaker cell (LaneRuntime, (pool,lane)-keyed) and the cell opens
capabilities.breaker-fastfail: a tripped target is refused before dispatch in milliseconds, not after the full timeout, via try_admit_breaker
capabilities.failover-reroute: a second interchangeable candidate is tried before the first byte, through ONE selection loop on every plane: failover::walk_with. It owns the whole decision -- is there a candidate set, is this hop a repeat and is that allowed, do the candidates' pins agree, will the breaker admit, and what the refusal is. A plane supplies exactly two values and no loop: the ORDER (which candidate is asked next) and the ADMISSION. MCP and A2A reach it via failover::walk (operator members: order, LaneRuntime::try_admit_breaker); the model plane reaches it via proxy::select::pick_among (SWRR / routing-policy / session-affinity order, LaneRuntime::try_admit -- the SAME breaker FSM, cell and single-flight probe, plus that plane's concurrency permit). The model plane's on_exhausted machinery (503 / fallback_pool / least_bad / queue, proxy/engine/walk.rs) is NOT selection: it is what that plane does after the one loop finds nothing, and it dispatches only through the loop's admission or its own documented least-bad breaker bypass
capabilities.hooks-tap: observe/transform hooks (rewrite, usage projection) run over the plane's payloads
capabilities.hooks-gate: hooks::gate::decide can refuse the plane's traffic before dispatch
capabilities.audit-chain: the plane's dispatches and refusals land in a tamper-evident hash chain (crate::audit)
capabilities.governance-budget: spend on the plane is attributed to the presenting key and budget limits refuse with a Retry-After
capabilities.disposition: the plane's upstream answers are normalized (Stage 1) and classified into Disposition (Stage 2, breaker::classify)
capabilities.metrics: the plane's traffic appears on the real /metrics scrape under its own plane label
capabilities.trust-pinning: the peer's artifact (schema digest / card fingerprint / SPKI) is pinned; drift is detected, demoted and refused
capabilities.net-guard: every outbound destination this role derives is SSRF-guarded through core net_guard (judged-address pinning, metadata refusal)
capabilities.egress-auth: outbound credentials are planned and injected by the one egress mechanism -- never a caller token passed through
capabilities.catalogue: what this caller may SEE is answered by the one core catalogue walk (catalogue::entitled), trust-gated per item

planes.llm: model traffic: app -> busbar -> provider, HTTP incl. SSE/binary streams (one plane, both halves)
planes.decisions: decision traffic: app -> busbar -> decision provider, outbound needs only (one direction, as llm): busbar's decisions front door served through its door, its far end the configured decision provider
planes.mcp-client: busbar's outbound leg to registered MCP servers -- streamable-HTTP and stdio; where the transport changes the answer, the cell's note says so
planes.mcp-server: busbar's MCP front door: inbound methods from clients and agents
planes.a2a-client: busbar issuing A2A requests: the relay leg to backend agents (JsonRpc, HttpJson, Grpc -- one relay below the transport axis), originate, card fetch
planes.a2a-server: busbar's A2A front door: inbound tasks/messages, plus this role's own outbound webhook push delivery
planes.streaming-client: busbar's outbound duplex leg: the dialed WSS to the realtime voice provider (OpenAI Realtime / Gemini Live) and the telephony media egress (Twilio g711); one session is pinned to one provider socket for its whole lifetime
planes.streaming-server: busbar's voice front door: inbound session-open ingress -- the browser sideband WebSocket and the telephony (Twilio) media-stream webhook -- that opens a governed duplex session

dialects.voice: the streaming plane's dialect (U14): it rides the streaming-client and streaming-server columns and is never a column of its own
